# Computer Science with Applications

> > A comprehensive textbook introducing computational thinking and programming fundamentals through Python, data structures, and practical applications.

This documentation site hosts the Computer Science with Applications textbook, designed for students learning programming basics through advanced topics like functional programming and data manipulation. The book emphasizes hands-on learning with real-world examples using Python, NumPy, and pandas.

## Key Topics

- Python
- Data Structures
- Functional Programming
- Recursion
- NumPy
- pandas
- Getting Started
- Control Flow
- Functions
- Exception Handling
- Classes and Objects
- Computational Thinking
- Code Organization
- CSV/JSON
- Educational Resource

## Core Chapters

- [Computer Science with Applications](https://book.cs-apps.org): Homepage for Computer Science with Applications textbook covering Python, NumPy, pandas
- [1. Getting Started](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/index.html): Getting Started chapter covering Python basics, control flow, functions, exceptions
- [2. Data Structures](https://book.cs-apps.org/data_structures/index.html): Data Structures chapter on lists, dicts, sets, stacks, queues, classes in Python
- [3. Functional Programming and Recursion](https://book.cs-apps.org/functions/index.html): Functional programming and recursion tutorial covering higher-order functions, trees
- [4. Working with Data](https://book.cs-apps.org/working_with_data/index.html): Working with Data chapter on NumPy, pandas, CSV, JSON file I/O and processing

## Programming Fundamentals

- [1.1. Computational Thinking](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/introduction/index.html): Computational thinking introduction with real-world examples and problem-solving
- [1.2. Programming Basics](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/basics/index.html): Programming Basics tutorial for Python 3 on Windows, MacOS, Linux platforms
- [1.3. Control Flow Statements](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/control_structures/index.html): Control Flow Statements tutorial covering conditionals, loops, and Python basics
- [1.4. Introduction to Functions](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/intro_functions/index.html): Introduction to Functions covering parameters, return values, code reuse in Python
- [1.6. Understanding Errors and Catching Exceptions](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/exceptions/index.html): Exception handling guide covering Python errors, stack traces, and error catching

## Data Structures & Object-Oriented Programming

- [2.1. Lists, Tuples, and Strings](https://book.cs-apps.org/data_structures/lists/index.html): Lists, Tuples, and Strings tutorial covering Python collections and sequences
- [2.2. Dictionaries and Sets](https://book.cs-apps.org/data_structures/dictionaries/index.html): Dictionaries and Sets tutorial on key-value storage and data organization in Python
- [2.3. Implementing a Data Structure: Stacks and Queues](https://book.cs-apps.org/data_structures/stacks_queues/index.html): Stacks and Queues implementation tutorial with API design and interfaces
- [2.4. Classes and Objects](https://book.cs-apps.org/data_structures/classes/index.html): Classes and Objects tutorial on OOP, encapsulation, and Python fundamentals

## Advanced Programming Concepts

- [3.1. Functional Programming](https://book.cs-apps.org/functions/functions/index.html): Functional Programming tutorial on higher-order functions and programming paradigms
- [3.2. Recursion](https://book.cs-apps.org/functions/recursion/index.html): Recursion tutorial covering base cases, recursive definitions, algorithm design

## Reference & Getting Started

- [Preface](https://book.cs-apps.org/preface.html): Preface introducing book notation, example code, and learning guide structure
- [1.5. Basics of Code Organization](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/organization/index.html): Code Organization tutorial on Python modules, imports, file structure fundamentals
- [1.7. Example: A Game of Chance](https://book.cs-apps.org/getting_started/example/index.html): Code example implementing a medieval dice game with probability and simulation
